doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Jazz education's growth, speed and the lack of communication
summary: They discuss the disconnect between jazz education and sales, and players focusing on exercises and fast playing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. It came off as spontaneous but was not. It was really arranged. What do you think, do you have an opinion if you observe what has happened to jazz education and its growth, I’m not sure I have a question here but I’m amazed at the level that jazz
education has risen to yet there seems to be a disconnect with record sales and just making a living as a jazz musician.

I agree. You know the music is getting so fast. It reflects the society we live in today. I mean you can do everything instantly rather than develop an emotion. People don’t have time. They don’t want to wait for the story and the conclusion, they just want to hear the conclusion. Oh my God. And that really annoys me. And no wonder the sales are down. It’s not communicating. Too many of these guys are playing the exercises. You know what I mean? [scats] “I bet I can play ‘Giant Steps’ faster than you.”
You can play it faster than me.
You know that kind of stuff, that stuff pisses me off, really.
Yeah. And my observation is, especially with the rhythm section players, is many people seem to be unsatisfied with just accompanying. It’s almost like everybody’s soloing at the same time.
